findings.F1: The Calmar fails because of one long fall. The book's yearly return is 21.5 % against a deepest fall of 40.6 % (Calmar 0.53 over 2898 days). That fall ran from w1 to w8 over 845 days, while holding the coins lost 67.3 %. The next falls, 32.2 % (w15 to w17) and 26.1 % (w18 to w19), also came while holding fell 42.3 % and 41.5 %.
findings.F2: The book loses on the bars where the coin's 20-day return is negative and gains only where it is positive. On held bars with a 20-day return below −8.75 %, the mean gain per bar is −0.020 % (t −0.42, n 1504); between −8.75 % and +0.5 % it is −0.009 % (t −0.16, n 1504); from +9.6 % to +24.5 % it is +0.40 % (t 4.23, n 1504).
findings.F3: The gain also depends on how near the coin is to its 60-day high. Held bars more than 25 % below that high earn −0.012 % a bar (t −0.34, n 1520), and those 13.5–25 % below earn +0.010 % (t 0.20). Bars within 2 % of the high earn +0.38 % (t 2.93) and bars 2–7 % below earn +0.30 % (t 3.62).
findings.F4: Combined, held bars with a positive 20-day return near the 60-day high carry a summed gain of 9.75 of the book's total 12.35, at a mean of +0.41 % a bar. Bars with a negative 20-day return far from the high sum to −0.61 (1811 bars), and those near the high to −0.32 (mean −0.27 %).
findings.F5: The book stays exposed after its signal is gone. It holds a position on 51 % of bars, and on 52 % of those held bars the forecast is already 0 or below; the mean gain is the same with or without a live forecast (+0.138 % against +0.141 %). The position therefore rides into the coin's later falls.
findings.F6: At entry, the longer trend sorts the trades. Trades entered with a 90-day return of 0 to 16.5 % lose 1.51 % on average after fees (38 % winners, n 127), and those at 16.5 to 34 % lose 2.33 % (39 % winners). Trades entered above 65 % gain 8.06 % (64 % winners, n 125).
findings.F7: The coin's recent 5-day path sorts the held bars the same way. Bars after a 5-day return below −4.7 % earn −0.059 % (t −1.27, n 1721), while bars after a 5-day return above +9 % earn +0.57 % (t 4.55, n 1721).
findings.F8: The size is not the binding problem. The total move per case is 4.9 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade (+0.95 % over 5 days), and the unusual move is 1.9 times that cost.

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 90-day return is not negative, a one-day rise that is large relative to its usual daily move (its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns) is followed by a further rise over the next 5 days, the larger that rise in units of the usual daily move, only while the coin's 20-day return is positive, and the more so the larger that 20-day return.
ideas.consequence: A trader keeps a long on a sharp up-day only while the coin's last 20 days are up, and sizes it with how far up they are, so the book is not long through the turn into a fall.
ideas.name: surges continue in 20-day uptrends

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 90-day return is not negative, a one-day rise that is large relative to its usual daily move (its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns) is followed by a further rise over the next 5 days, the larger that rise in units of the usual daily move, and the more so the closer the coin's close is to its highest close of the past 60 days.
ideas.consequence: A sharp up-day near the coin's 60-day high is a reason to go long for the following days, while the same up-day deep below that high is a reason to refuse the trade.
ideas.name: surges near highs continue

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 90-day return is not negative, a one-day rise that is large relative to its usual daily move (its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns) is followed by a further rise over the next 5 days, the larger that rise in units of the usual daily move, and the more so the larger the coin's 90-day return.
ideas.consequence: A trader leans harder on sharp up-days in coins with a strong 90-day rise, and holds back in coins that are only slightly up over 90 days.
ideas.name: surges scale with 90-day trend
